facts.raw_span: subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts
subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts

concepts.why: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions, nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, and a high percentage of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis are indicative of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
The violaceous cutaneous lesions and restriction of diffusion in the cutaneous scalp are characteristic of Leukemia Cutis.

aliases: Lymphomatous Involvement of the Nervous System
concepts.why: The severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots suggest Neurolymphomatosis.
The presence of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis and the nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots are indicative of Meningeal Carcinomatosis.
The severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots suggest Spinal Cord Compression.
The presence of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis and the nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots are indicative of Leptomeningeal Disease.
The severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots suggest Cauda Equina Syndrome.
The presence of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis and the nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots are indicative of Lymphomatous Meningitis.

rationales.F01: Subacute progressive symmetric lower extremity weakness is more typical of Leptomeningeal Disease and Spinal Cord Compression.
rationales.F04: Severe flaccid quadriparesis is a strong indicator of Leptomeningeal Disease, Spinal Cord Compression, and Lymphomatous Meningitis.
rationales.F06: Violaceous cutaneous lesions are highly suggestive of Leukemia Cutis.
rationales.F09: Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots is more typical of Leptomeningeal Disease and Spinal Cord Compression.
rationales.F11: Cell differential showing 98% atypical cells/blasts is highly suggestive of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia and Leptomeningeal Disease.
